result.title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation
result.summary: Neural theorem proving increasingly uses retrieved premises and project context to support proof generation. Evaluating these resources requires measuring the advantage of target-selected declarations over comparable alternatives and how this advantage depends on training. We introduce LeanContext, a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof generation problems, to investigate these questions. We group selected complete preceding mathematical declarations as Mathematical Context (MC) and the remaining selected local source commands as Environment Context (EC). Four aligned input views support crossed training and inference evaluations with shared targets and original Lean verification environments. For both diffusion- and autoregressive-based models, selected declarations outperform comparable alternatives by a larger margin when training includes MC. Final-input audits identify omitted declarations referenced by the target. Prioritizing these dependencies improves Pass@32 by 1.40% and 1.70% for LLaDA and Llama, respectively, on 2,000 targets. The selection experiment operates without access to target reference proofs and holds checkpoints, EC, and inference budgets constant. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/haaaardcvZ/LeanContext.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LeanContext——129,826 道 Lean 整证明生成问题的基准，将目标选中的数学声明（MC）与剩余局部环境命令（EC）分组，用四个对齐输入视角做训练/推理交叉评测，衡量目标相关声明相对可比替代项的增益，并审计被目标引用却遗漏的声明。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定其他条件、交叉训练/推理视角」以归属某类输入贡献的方法，可能可供核查 LVR 中必要视觉证据与干扰上下文的分离及贡献分配；但领域为形式化证明，无视觉或多模态状态生成，联系尚属类比。
